title: How screen time can change your mood

explain.say: Have you ever looked up from a screen to find two hours had vanished, and you felt a bit grumpy? Screens are not good or bad by themselves. It depends how you use them. Look at the two sides on the board.

explain.say: The trick is to notice how you feel after using a screen. If you feel drained, swap some time for a walk, a friend or a book. Well done! Challenge: after screen time this week, ask yourself, "Did that lift me or drain me?"

faq.q: Can screen time be good for you?
faq.a: Yes. Talking to family far away, learning skills, being creative and sharing a film with others can all lift your mood. It is about what you do and how much.

faq.q: Why do I feel grumpy after lots of screen time?
faq.a: Long screen time often means less sleep, less moving and more comparing yourself with others. The quick buzz also fades, which can leave you feeling flat.
asks: Why do I feel bad after scrolling?

faq.q: Why is it so hard to stop scrolling?
faq.a: New posts give your brain small bursts of dopamine, a feel-good chemical, and endless feeds never run out. That makes it easy to keep going without deciding to.

faq.q: How much screen time is okay?
faq.a: There is no single number for everyone. A good balance leaves plenty of time for sleep, moving, schoolwork and people, with screens out of the bedroom at night. Agree limits with your family.
asks: How many hours of screens is too many?

faq.q: What if something online upsets me?
faq.a: Stop looking, do not reply, and tell a trusted grown-up straight away. You can also block and report the account. It is never your fault.
asks: Someone was mean to me online

facts: Many apps use features like endless scrolling and autoplay, which make it easy to keep watching without deciding to.
The World Health Organization advises that children under 2 should have no sedentary screen time, and children aged 2 to 4 no more than one hour a day.
